paragraphs.text: Orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18) is a form of oral-facial-digital syndrome with skeletal dysplasia. Oral anomalies include supernumerary frenulae, missing incisors and median clefting of the upper lip. Digital anomalies include brachydactyly with shortening of the middle phalanges, postaxial polydactyly of the hands and preaxial polydactyly of the feet. Patients also have short stature and short femoral necks, without rib shortening or a narrow thorax, and intelligence is normal (Thevenon et al., 2016).

paragraphs.text: Phadke et al. (1999) described a consanguineous family with a new variety of oral-facial-digital syndrome (OFDS) with oral, facial and digital malformations, acromelic short stature and genu valgum. They noted that these features overlapped with Ellis-van Creveld syndrome (EVCS). One of the sibs also had urinary incontinence and growth hormone deficiency, which the authors stated had not been reported before in any type of OFDS.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) restudied the consanguineous Indian family reported by Phadke et al. (1999), in which 3 sibs were affected. Subject II-1, a male examined at 25 years of age, had normal intelligence. His final height was 155 cm (-3 SD) and his weight was 45 kg (<-3 SD). He had a square face, short forehead, upslanting palpebral fissures, high nasal bridge, pyriform nose, short philtrum and medial clefting of the upper lip. Oral anomalies were supernumerary frenulae and missing incisors. Digital anomalies included pronounced brachydactyly, postaxial polydactyly of the upper limbs and a gap between the first and second toes. Radiographs showed severe shortening of the middle phalanges of the hands and feet, and preaxial foot polydactyly with duplication of the first metatarsal. Bone studies showed bilateral short femoral necks with varus femurs, symmetric genu valgum and no vertebral anomalies. Heart, renal and abdominal ultrasound examinations were normal.

paragraphs.text: Subject II-2 in the family studied by Thevenon et al. (2016), a female examined at 22 years of age, had normal intelligence. She was married with no children. Her final height was 122 cm (-5 SD) and her weight was 37 kg (-2 SD). She had a square face, narrow forehead, enophthalmia, upslanting palpebral fissures and a broad nasal bridge. She also had bilateral hypopigmented pseudoclefts with medial labial clefting, missing incisors and supernumerary oral frenulae. Digital anomalies included marked brachydactyly and postaxial polydactyly of all 4 limbs, which was surgically removed in infancy. Hand radiographs showed shortening of the middle phalanges, fused proximal phalanges and bifid distal phalanges. Foot radiographs showed duplication of the first metatarsal and absent intermediate phalanges, suggesting preaxial polydactyly. She had abnormal vertebral bodies with medial notches but no platyspondyly, bilateral cervical ribs without a narrow thorax, gracile long bones and shortened femoral necks. She had no dolichostenomelia and no delayed puberty. Brain MRI and abdominal and heart ultrasounds were normal. The third affected sib, subject II-3, died at 17 years of age from a complicated pulmonary infection.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied 3 sibs from a consanguineous Indian family with an unclassified OFDS with short stature and brachymesophalangia, originally reported by Phadke et al. (1999). Exome sequencing within the homozygous intervals identified a homozygous synonymous variant in the IFT57 gene, a c.777G-A transition (lys259-to-lys; K259K) at the last base of exon 6. Sanger sequencing confirmed that all 3 affected sibs were homozygous for the variant. The variant was absent from the ExAC database and from 50 healthy controls from northern India. In patient fibroblasts, the mutation caused a complex splicing pattern. Alongside the normal transcript there were 3 abnormal mRNAs: in-frame skipping of exon 6, in-frame skipping of exons 5 and 6, and out-of-frame skipping of exons 4 to 6. The abnormal transcripts were detected only after inhibition of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD), and total IFT57 mRNA was significantly reduced.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) found that cilia in fibroblasts from patients with OFD18 were normal in number and length, but anterograde ciliary transport was impaired. IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip was significantly decreased (90% vs 35%), and staining at the basal body was increased. SAG-induced GLI1 expression was poor in patient fibroblasts. In control fibroblasts, siRNA knockdown of IFT57 abolished SAG-induced GLI1 expression, pointing to defective SHH signaling.

checks.claim: Cilia in fibroblasts from patients with OFD18 were normal in number and length.
checks.evidence_quote: Primary cilia number and length in fibroblasts from the subject with the IFT57 mutation were similar to those in controls

checks.claim: Anterograde ciliary transport was impaired in fibroblasts from patients with OFD18.
checks.evidence_quote: Immunofluorescence showing decreased anterograde ciliary transport in the subject’s fibroblasts.

checks.claim: IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip was significantly decreased in OFD18 patient fibroblasts compared with controls (90% vs 35%).
checks.evidence_quote: In the subject’s fibroblasts, staining of the ciliary tip with IFT57 was significantly decreased (90% versus 35%; p<0.001)

checks.claim: IFT57 staining at the basal body was increased in OFD18 patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: while staining of the basal body of the primary cilium was significantly increased (p<0.01)

checks.claim: SAG-induced GLI1 expression was poor in OFD18 patient fibroblasts.
checks.evidence_quote: Stimulation of the SHH pathway by Smoothened Agonist (SAG) showed poor induction of Gli1 mRNA expression in fibroblasts from the IFT57-mutated subject compared with control fibroblasts

checks.claim: siRNA knockdown of IFT57 in control fibroblasts abolished SAG-induced GLI1 expression.
checks.evidence_quote: whereas no induction of Gli1 mRNA expression was observed in siRNA IFT57-transfected cells

checks.claim: The GLI1 expression findings point to defective SHH signaling in OFD18.
checks.evidence_quote: This indicates that even though ciliary assembly is normal in these cells the reduction in IFT57 causes dysfunctional SHH signaling.

paragraphs.text: Thevenon et al. (2016) studied 3 affected sibs from a consanguineous Indian family with orofaciodigital syndrome XVIII (OFD18), originally reported by Phadke et al. (1999). All 3 were homozygous for a c.777G-A transition in the IFT57 gene at the last base of exon 6, a synonymous change (lys259-to-lys; K259K). The mutation was found by exome sequencing within homozygous intervals and confirmed by Sanger sequencing. It was absent from the ExAC database and from 50 healthy controls from northern India. In patient fibroblasts, the mutation caused in-frame skipping of exon 6, in-frame skipping of exons 5 and 6, and out-of-frame skipping of exons 4 to 6, alongside the normal transcript. The abnormal transcripts were detected only after NMD inhibition, and total IFT57 mRNA was significantly reduced. Patient fibroblasts showed decreased IFT57 staining at the ciliary tip and defective SHH signaling.
